Fury: finite, smooth trailing edges

The preserved Fury_RC_TE_0p5in.ntop revision has 0.5-inch (12.7 mm) total trailing-edge thickness on the wing, horizontal stabilizer, and vertical stabilizer. A native C2 Ramp changes the aft 25% of each chord. This is the selected Fury geometry reference for this collection.

The report below also records later mesh trials and unresolved defects. A smooth native edge does not establish a qualified CFD mesh. Earlier thin-edge figures in the development history are labelled as previous trials.

Prism and tetrahedron fallback: small pipeline passes

A resolved synthetic annular duct produces 33,239 tetrahedra and 9,216 prisms. All strict OpenFOAM topology and geometry checks pass with the same quality limits. A conservative startup run completes 200 iterations in 9.98 seconds. This verifies the small pipeline only. It does not establish aircraft performance or convergence. The first startup attempt failed on negative temperature at iteration four. The successful retry uses first-order convection and lower relaxation factors.

Synthetic pipeline audit.

A separate test disables boundary reconnection explicitly. All 3,072 wall triangles and 1,536 wall vertices match the input exactly. All wall faces receive three prism layers. The resulting 41,533 cells pass both standard and strict OpenFOAM checks. The earlier test retained vertices but reconnected 92 boundary facets. Exact-boundary and layer audit; Strict conversion and volume qualification.

02Verify native nTop surface export

The export notebook adds native mesh and STL export blocks to a separate copy. Recorded native block catalogs and implementation source define the input order.

The dependency pruning retains the selected exterior assembly. Internal allocation bodies and deployed gear are excluded from the aircraft export.

nTop exports STL coordinates in millimeters. The surface checker writes a separate meter copy with a factor of 0.001.

The sphere's measured extents test that scale directly. A successful sphere export does not establish aircraft mesh quality or inlet connectivity.

Dual contouring uses minimum feature size and adaptivity. It has no direct surface-deviation tolerance input. Adaptivity zero disables decimation.

The native block description permits self-intersections and non-manifold output. Each completed DC surface therefore needs its own topology and self-intersection checks.

Check the final field multiplier

A separate 4 mm strip changes only the final positive field multiplier from 0.25 to 1. That operation preserves the field sign and zero surface. Bounds and the other meshing settings remain unchanged.

The changed-factor strip has 19,008 triangles and 8.737763 mm maximum sampled trailing-edge recession. The previous 0.25-factor result was 8.712676 mm. The multiplier does not cure this defect. Native field-factor result.

Refine the measured worst-edge neighborhood

The full-width 1 mm strip timed out without an STL. A separate local comparison uses a smaller region around the worst previously measured 2 mm edge station.

The region was selected before either local export. Both variants retain the same cropped geometry and settings. Only mesh resolution and the output path change.

The small 1 mm adaptive fixture without remeshing has three independent intersection reports on its cut boundaries. It is not an accepted surface. The larger 4 mm strip has a separate small component and fails the edge screen.

The small remeshed variant passes the independent intersection check. The finer full-strip remesh trial changes both tolerance and remeshing. It does not isolate each setting's effect.

These results do not establish an aircraft export speedup. The full 2 mm voxel export remains a separate bounded run. Native completion and a closed edge count do not replace the independent intersection check.

Three multi-region fixtures add a native trailing-edge feature plane. Each fails during loading, before meshing. The first reports a version/load error; the next two report a deserializer assertion. Correcting the vector literal format before the third attempt does not resolve the load failure. These are authoring/runtime failures, with no surface result.

The fourth multi-region fixture uses the documented native None input sentinel. It completes after this authoring correction and passes the independent intersection check. Its 3.896774 mm local edge error does not show an improvement over the earlier local adaptive fixture. No larger feature-constrained export is approved from this result.

An explicit 2 mm maximum edge size also gives no improvement: the local maximum error is 3.933476 mm. A guarded gradient-normalization fixture preserves the underlying field graph but changes its numerical values. It reaches its 60-second bound without an STL. A second fixture restores the original explicit bounding box. That fixture also reaches its 60-second bound without an STL. Their finite-field and geometry checks remain incomplete.

The remeshed adaptive strip is closed, oriented, vertex-manifold, and independently free of reported intersections. However, its Euler characteristic is -148, corresponding to genus75 for its single component. The voxel strip has Euler characteristic2.

This additional topology and visual check rejects the adaptive strip. The result does not prove a defect in the native implicit field. These results do not support a full-aircraft AT export. Reviewed topology evidence.

The audit measures 614,685 wall vertices and arithmetic face centers. The maximum nearest-STL distance is 10.705734 mm. The RMS is 0.128735 mm, and the 95th percentile is 0.141438 mm.

This is a one-way finite comparison with the exact input STL. It does not establish agreement with the native CAD surface. Distance evidence.

A separate direct calculation checks the maximum point against every input triangle. It returns 10.705734 mm, with a difference of 0 m from the VTK result. Independent peak check.

The standard check uses allTopology and meshQuality. The stricter check also uses allGeometry and reports concave cells.

A concave-cell count is a face-plane diagnostic. It does not, by itself, mean that cells have negative volume. The measured minimum volumes are listed separately.

Strict failures remain unresolved. Positive cell volume and passing configured face criteria do not override the current strict acceptance gate.

A passing mesh-quality log does not establish physical accuracy or mesh convergence. Compare multiple completed aircraft meshes before using a flow solution for a design decision.

05Keep the acceptance stages separate

StageRequired evidenceCurrent scope
Native pipelineCompleted export log, output notebook hash, readable STL, and measured unitsThe sphere tests export mechanics. Aircraft surfaces need their own checks.
Aircraft surfaceSource identity, topology, inlet/exit openings, thin edges, and mesh-size comparisonA closed triangulated body does not prove that its intended passages remain open.
Aircraft volumeCompleted mesher and checkMesh outputs, connected fluid region, local refinement, and actual layer coverageSynthetic smoke results cannot accept aircraft cells.
Flow solutionDefined operating conditions, boundary conditions, convergence, and mesh sensitivityNo flow solution is included in this report.

The 16 ft RC span and 200 mph speed belong to the broader design study. This supplement does not derive wall spacing or a turbulence model from those values.

The initial planned RANS treatment uses wall functions, pending the optional user preference. No computed y+ values are available. A future solution must check the actual distribution with the OpenFOAM yPlus function before accepting wall spacing.

The internal engine allocation is not an installed propulsion model. Mesh preparation does not establish engine mass flow or thermal clearance.

06Reproduce and inspect the evidence

The generator reads prepared variants, local logs, and actual STL files. It does not execute nTop, OpenFOAM meshers, or a flow solver.
